name: application-recipe-step-card
title: Recipe Step Card
description: Numbered cooking step with instructions, an image, and a real start/pause/reset countdown timer that ticks via an interval and stops itself at zero.
useWhen: Walking a user through a single recipe step at a time where a specific step benefits from an active countdown (simmering, baking, resting).
The timer should be genuinely interactive (start/pause/reset), not a static duration label.
Each step benefits from a numbered badge over an image to visually anchor progress through the recipe.
avoidWhen: You're building a sequential list of lessons/videos to play through — use `lesson-playlist` for that playlist-navigation pattern instead.
The step has no timed component — drop the timer control and use a simpler numbered instruction card.
Multiple timers need to run simultaneously across steps — coordinate state at a parent level rather than duplicating this card blindly.
responsiveBehavior: Fixed-width card (max-w-sm) with an aspect-video image; instructions text wraps naturally and the timer control row stays a fixed height.
accessibility: The Start/Pause button label always reflects real running state, and disables itself once the timer reaches zero rather than allowing a no-op restart.
Timer time is rendered as monospaced, tabular-nums text so digits don't shift width as they change.
Reset returns the timer to its original duration and stopped state in one action, matching the visible 'Reset' label.

variants.title: Recipe Step Card
variants.description: Step 3 of a recipe with an 8-minute simmer timer; Start begins a real countdown, Pause halts it, Reset restores 08:00.
accessibility: Timer countdown is driven by a real interval and the Start/Pause button label and disabled state are derived from the same running/remaining values.

variants.title: Recipe Step Card (Dark)
variants.description: Recipe step card adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: Timer and button colors are tuned to meet WCAG AA contrast against the dark surface.
